Q: What is the significance of making a nested function global in Lua? A:

I looked at the Wikipedia article and your code, and I don't have a clue what that algorithm is doing, but I do know how defining Lua functions work. (don't know whether this will help or not)

there are two ways: local and global. Even when you define function B inside function A, if you don't put local in front of the definition, B is a global variable.

The other thing is upvalues. Every time Lua's control flow passes through a function definition, it creates a new "instance" of the function, with the upvalues captured in that function (if there are any upvalues).(more info: https://www.lua.org/pil/6.1.html)

In your code, when B is defined as a global function, the global variable "B" is overwritten every time you call A. Then any further calls to B will call the latest definition of "B".

But when B is defined as a local function, it does not overwrite previous "instances" of B. Then any further calls to B depend on which instance of B is referenced.

Q: Python/selenium how to use proxy with undetected-chromedriver A:

I assume you set up a green flag for your machine on your server, so you don't need to enter the login and password for the server:

options.add_argument('--proxy-server=185.195.81.152:12573') 
options.add_argument('--proxy-server=socks5://185.195.81.152:12573') # socks5
options.add_argument('--proxy-server=https://185.195.81.152:12573') # https

also suggest using:

options.add_argument('--proxy-bypass-list=<-loopback>')

If you didn't green flag your machines IP to the server, then you'll need to provide the login and password as well:

options.add_argument('--proxy-server=proxy_username:proxy_password@proxy_ip:proxy_port')

Q: How to return to the same scroll position when going back using useNavigate() or useLocation() react-router A:

You can check browser history API https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/History#specifications

Or you can get the current scroll position before navigating and then reset it when you return.

window.pageYOffset || document.documentElement.scrollTop - This should get you current scroll position

Q: What are the default font sizes (in pixels) for the html heading tags (<h1>, <h2>, <h3>, etc.)? A:

This is set in the browser's default stylesheet. As of 2023, modern browsers all set these to the same em values. And, by default, 1em is 16px in modern browsers, thus:

H𝑛 em px
h1 2em 32px
h2 1.5em 24px
h3 1.17em 18.72px
h4 1em 16px
h5 0.83em 13.28px
h6 0.67em 10.72px

These values are what the WhatWG's living standard recommends and I checked that Chrome, Firefox and Safari indeed implement these values.

(Note that the values for h5 and h6 are slightly different than in the legacy default style sheet for HTML 4).

Finally, you can run the following snippet, then inspect in your browser of choice:

<h1>h1</h1>
<h2>h2</h2>
<h3>h3</h3>
<h4>h4</h4>
<h5>h5</h5>
<h6>h6</h6>

Q: Javascript toString quirk A:

toString doesn't accept arguments, so toString(fn) is the same as just toString(), which returns an implicit global object, converted to string. toString.call(fn) calls the global object’s .toString passing a function object as this, but since that .toString is a method of Object, the result is different from Function.prototype.toString.

Q: How to access slide notes reliably from a BASIC macro A:

Working code example to extract the notes text from slide 1


Sub ExtractFirstSlideNotes
    Dim oDoc As Object
    Dim oSlideList As Object
    Dim oSlide As Object
    Dim oNotesPage As Object
    Dim oShape As Object
    Dim sNotes As String
    Dim i As Integer

    oDoc = ThisComponent
    oSlideList = oDoc.getDrawPages()

    If oSlideList.getCount() = 0 Then
        MsgBox "No slides in presentation."
        Exit Sub
    End If

    oSlide = oSlideList.getByIndex(0)
    oNotesPage = oSlide.getNotesPage()

    sNotes = ""
    For i = 0 To oNotesPage.getCount() - 1
        oShape = oNotesPage.getByIndex(i)
        If Not IsNull(oShape) Then
            If oShape.supportsService("com.sun.star.drawing.TextShape") Then
                sNotes = sNotes & oShape.getString() & Chr(10)
            End If
        End If
    Next i

    If Len(Trim(sNotes)) > 0 Then
        MsgBox "Notes from First Slide:" & Chr(13) & sNotes
    Else
        MsgBox "No text found in notes."
    End If
End Sub
